facts.content: Patient reports decreased hearing in the left ear for 6 weeks.
Patient experiences intermittent tinnitus in the left ear, associated with TV/music.
facts.source_text: Intermittent tinnitus L; assoc. with TV/music

facts.content: Patient reports mild intermittent dizziness and a feeling of being off-balance, without true vertigo or nausea provocation.
facts.source_text: Mild intermittent dizziness/off-balance; no true vertigo; not nausea-provoked

facts.content: Patient had a prior brief episode of decreased hearing about 1 year ago which self-resolved in days.
facts.source_text: Prior brief episode ~1 yr ago (self-resolved in days)

facts.content: Patient reports no ear pain (otalgia), chest pain (CP), or fever.
facts.source_text: No otalgia. No CP. No fever.

facts.content: Left-sided hearing difficulty for 6 weeks with intermittent tinnitus and mild disequilibrium, no ear pain or fever, right ear unaffected.
facts.source_text: L-sided hearing difficulty x6 wks with intermittent tinnitus and mild disequilibrium. No otalgia/fever. R ear unaffected.

facts.content: Needs otoscopic exam to rule out impacted cerumen versus middle/inner ear/balance pathology.
facts.source_text: Needs otoscopic exam to r/o impacted cerumen vs middle/inner ear/balance pathology.

facts.content: Book face-to-face ear exam in 4–5 days to inspect the ear canal and tympanic membrane, rule out wax or obstruction.
facts.source_text: Book F2F ear exam in 4–5 days to inspect canal/TM; r/o wax/obstruction.

facts.content: Administration to arrange and patient to call support line to schedule.
facts.source_text: Admin to arrange; pt to call support line as per note to schedule.

facts.content: Provide patient with a tinnitus information leaflet link to review before the visit.
facts.source_text: Provide tinnitus info leaflet link; pt to review before visit.

facts.content: Safety-net information: not an emergency. If symptoms worsen or new issues arise before appointment, book another video consult.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: Not emergent. If symptoms worsen or new issues arise before appt, book another video consult.
